input: Research local ice climbing introductory sessions

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: Ice climbing is highly location-dependent — knowing the user's city or region determines which venues, guides, and outdoor sites are even relevant to research.
Whether this is for the user alone, a group, or a specific person (e.g. a gift) changes what session formats and group sizes to look for.
Ice climbing is seasonal; knowing when they want to go narrows which sessions are currently bookable and whether artificial vs. natural ice is needed.
Introductory sessions vary widely in cost (gear rental, guide fees, travel); a budget ceiling rules out certain options immediately.
The user may want only outdoor natural-ice experiences, only indoor climbing walls with ice simulation, or both — this fundamentally shapes which venues to include.

Some users prioritise safety and instructor credentials, others care more about the social/adventure atmosphere, and others want the shortest possible commitment — this shapes how to rank and present options.
Knowing what 'done well' looks like — a shortlist of 3 bookable options, a comparison table, or a single recommendation — determines how deep and what format the research output should take.

gold.taskTitle: Research local ice climbing intro sessions
gold.taskDescription: Find and evaluate introductory ice climbing sessions available in the user's local area.

questions.title: What city or region should the search focus on?
questions.description: Identify the user's location so only geographically relevant venues, outdoor sites, and guide services are included in the research.

questions.title: Is this for you alone, or others too?
questions.description: Determine whether the session is for a solo participant, a pair, or a larger group, which affects format, pricing tiers, and private vs. group session options.

questions.title: What timeframe are you hoping to attend a session?
questions.description: Pin down the target dates or season so the research reflects currently available bookings and accounts for seasonal ice conditions.

questions.title: What is your rough budget per person for the session?
questions.description: Establish a spending ceiling to filter out options that include gear rental, guide fees, or travel costs beyond what the user is willing to pay.

questions.title: Do you want outdoor natural ice, indoor ice walls, or both?
questions.description: Clarify whether the search should cover real outdoor ice climbing sites, indoor/artificial ice facilities, or all options regardless of setting.

questions.title: What matters most to you when choosing a session?
questions.description: Understand the user's top priority — such as instructor certification, adventure atmosphere, minimal time commitment, or beginner-friendliness — to rank results accordingly.

questions.title: What should the final research output look like?
questions.description: Determine the desired deliverable — e.g. a shortlist of bookable options, a side-by-side comparison, or a single top recommendation — so the depth and format of research matches expectations.
